cases.name: checkpoint-127.ots
cases.range: through the newline that terminates the blank separator line
cases.says: SPEC 6: the stamped value is SHA-256 of the note's leading bytes through the blank separator line -- the three body lines PLUS the blank line, four 0x0A in all. Not the three-line body, and not SPEC 7's signed text, which stops one 0x0A earlier. Those are three different byte ranges

cases.name: sample.ots
cases.says: a proof over an arbitrary digest, deliberately unrelated to this fixture: it exercises the parser against bytes neither Norn implementation wrote. Nothing in the suite produces this digest -- the file states it

comment: OpenTimestamps proofs, written by `python-opentimestamps`. Anchoring is advisory (D-009), so a reader that computes the wrong byte range never matches a stamp and never says so -- which is why the digest is stated here rather than left to be derived. `calendar-response.bin` is what POST <calendar>/digest returns for the checkpoint digest above: a bare timestamp tree with no file header
